c1-29-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Is the Picture Genuine?
c1-29-01.scenario: A friend visits the National Museum with you and asks whether a picture on display can be trusted.
c1-29-01.prompt: Tell your friend that the documents are authentic as far as the picture's origin goes, and that the repair can be reversed.
cues: Say what the documents show about the picture's origin
Say how the repair looks from a conservator's point of view
c1-29-01.target: A kép provenienciáját tekintve minden dokumentum hiteles. Restaurátori szempontból a javítás reverzibilis.
c1-29-01.english: As for the picture's provenance, every document is authentic. From a conservator's point of view the repair is reversible.
c1-29-01.canDo: I can judge a museum object from one viewpoint with *jogi szempontból* or *restaurátori szempontból*.

c1-29-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Respecting the Layers
c1-29-02.scenario: A friend asks what a restorer should do with an old church wall that later builders changed.
c1-29-02.prompt: Tell your friend that a good restoration keeps the historical layers, and name the procedure that puts fallen stones back.
cues: Say what kind of restoration keeps the historical layers
Name the procedure that puts the original stones back
c1-29-02.target: A rétegeket tiszteletben tartó felújítás megőrzi a hitelességet. Az eredeti köveket visszahelyező eljárás neve anasztilózis.
c1-29-02.english: A restoration that respects the layers keeps authenticity. The procedure that puts the original stones back is called anastylosis.
c1-29-02.canDo: I can describe a restoration with a participle before the noun, as in *a rétegeket tiszteletben tartó felújítás*.

c1-29-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Copy or Original?
c1-29-03.scenario: A friend asks you whether a rebuilt facade is as good as the old stone.
c1-29-03.prompt: Tell your friend that the copy is beautiful but not authentic, and that the original stone is a witness of its time.
cues: Admit that the copy is beautiful, then add a reservation
Contrast the copy with the original stone
c1-29-03.target: A másolat szép, mindazonáltal nem hiteles. A másolattal szemben az eredeti kő a kor tanúja.
c1-29-03.english: The copy is beautiful; nevertheless it is not authentic. As against the copy, the original stone is a witness of its time.
c1-29-03.canDo: I can contrast an original with a copy using *a másolattal szemben*.

c1-29-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why a Memorial?
c1-29-04.scenario: A friend asks you why a town puts up a memorial and why the museum stays open.
c1-29-04.prompt: Tell your friend why the memorial is put up and why the museum is open.
cues: Give the purpose of the memorial
Give the purpose of keeping the museum open
c1-29-04.target: Emlékhelyet állítanak abból a célból, hogy ne felejtsük el a múltat. A múzeum azért tart nyitva, hogy mindenki megnézhesse a gyűjteményt.
c1-29-04.english: A memorial is put up so that we do not forget the past. The museum is open so that everyone can see the collection.
c1-29-04.canDo: I can give a formal purpose with *abból a célból, hogy*.

c1-29-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Museum Gave
c1-29-05.scenario: A friend has read about Pulszky Ferenc and asks what a public museum gave to the citizens.
c1-29-05.prompt: Tell your friend what the public museum gave to the citizens and what longer opening hours did.
cues: Say how much the museum enriched the citizens' lives
Say what longer opening hours did to the number of visitors
c1-29-05.target: A nyilvános múzeum felbecsülhetetlen mértékben gazdagította a polgárok életét. A nyitva tartás számottevően megnövelte a látogatók számát.
c1-29-05.english: The public museum enriched the citizens' lives to an immeasurable degree. Longer opening hours markedly increased the number of visitors.
c1-29-05.canDo: I can say how much an institution changed things with *számottevően* or *felbecsülhetetlen mértékben*.

c1-29-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Museum
c1-29-consolidation.scenario: At the end of a visit to the National Museum, a friend asks what you learned about museums and monuments.
c1-29-consolidation.prompt: Tell your friend what a good restoration keeps, what the copy lacks, and what the public museum gave to the citizens.
cues: Say what a good restoration respects
Say what the copy lacks compared with the original
Say what the public museum gave to the citizens
c1-29-consolidation.target: A rétegeket tiszteletben tartó felújítás megőrzi a hitelességet. A másolattal szemben az eredeti kő a kor tanúja. A nyilvános múzeum felbecsülhetetlen mértékben gazdagította a polgárok életét.
c1-29-consolidation.english: A restoration that respects the layers keeps authenticity. As against the copy, the original stone is a witness of its time. The public museum enriched the citizens' lives to an immeasurable degree.
c1-29-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words of provenance research, monument protection and cultural memory.
